newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak NPF says has no word on EBRD Slovnaft stake.
newsitem.headline: Slovak NPF says has no word on EBRD Slovnaft stake.

text.p: The Slovak privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), said on Tuesday it had not received instructions from the government to buy back a stake in crude oil refiner Slovnaft from the EBRD.

Last week, Jiri Huebner, head of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) Czech and Slovak team, told Reuters that the bank was expecting a proposal from the NPF to "buy out" its share after recent encouragement from the Finance Ministry to do so.

"If the ministry said so we should probably soon receive some instructions on it, but as far as I know it has not happened yet," Jan Kato, an NPF executive director and chairman of the Slovnaft Supervisory Board, told Reuters.
"Of course, the matter is somehow developing further, ... but the decision is probably far off."
The EBRD took a 10.5 percent stake in Slovnaft over a year ago when it bought a half of its unsuccessful $113 million Global Depositary Receipt (GDR) issue.

Soon after the acquisition, the NPF sold a 39 percent stake in the refiner to management-led group Slovintegra at a deep discount compared to the GDR price. This led to several rounds of talks between the EBRD and NPF.
When asked whether the NPF could afford to buy the EBRD stake back, Kato said: "The Fund is perpetual and bottomless".

Market analysts widely believe the NPF lacks liquidity due to its focus on direct sales to mainly "domestic owners". These sales are often at large discounts, and with a payment calender spread over several years.

As for the NPF's remaining 25 percent in Slovnaft, Kato said the fund was still preparing its already announced plan to exchange shares in the refiner for the privatisation bonds which were issued by the government to citizens.
The NPF has recently offered stakes in several minor issues in exchange for the privatisation bonds, but the Slovnaft offer would mark the most prominent firm in the NPF's programme thus far.
